thread:
emma: heads up — after the homebrew upgrade on my M1, redwoodctl stopped picking up my local profile. localserve says "no auth token found" even though ~/.config/redwood/profile.toml exists. anyone seen this?

raj: hmm, did you install via brew or the pkg? on M1 homebrew path is /opt/homebrew so symlinks sometimes point to the intel path.

emma: installed with `brew upgrade redwoodctl` this morning. i suspect the completion/symlink hooks changed. `which redwoodctl` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl, but the postinstall wrote config to /usr/local/etc/redwood which my localserve doesn't check.

kelly: ouch. quick check: try `REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR=~/.config/redwood redwoodctl localserve --profile default` — localserve honours REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR if explicitly set.

emma: tried that, localserve works when i force REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR. login flow still flaky though: `redwoodctl login` hangs after opening browser. looks like the credential helper path the binary expects is mismatched.

raj: can you paste the output of `redwoodctl info --diagnose`? (redact tokens)

emma: pasted below (sanitized):
```
redwoodctl version: 0.21.4
install_method: brew
binary_path: /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl
config_path: /usr/local/etc/redwood
profile_dir: ~/.config/redwood
credential_helper: /usr/local/bin/rdw-cred-helper
```
localserve error: "failed to load profile: file not found /usr/local/etc/redwood/profile.toml"
```

kelly: yep, credential_helper path points to /usr/local which doesn't exist on fresh ARM installs. the brew postinstall should have created a symlink but didn't when the upgrade came from a cask -> brew split.

devex-bot: @emma I filed a ticket #DEVEX-4822 for the postinstall symlink issue; tag: install/macos/homebrew.

emma: thanks. workaround i used locally: `ln -s /opt/homebrew/etc/redwood /usr/local/etc/redwood` and `ln -s /opt/homebrew/bin/rdw-cred-helper /usr/local/bin/rdw-cred-helper` — then restart shell and `redwoodctl login` completed. not ideal though.

raj: can we have `redwoodctl` check both /usr/local and /opt/homebrew paths at runtime? Or fall back to looking up relative to `binary_path`? fallback would reduce these hacks.

kelly: agree. defensive lookup + a one-time migration message during `redwoodctl upgrade` would help. i can draft a tiny PR to try both locations and print a clear hint when mismatch detected.

sre-jan: also consider editing the brew formula postinstall to create the symlinks when HOME is ARM. that avoids user tinkering. i'll coordinate with distro.

emma: created a tiny gist with the minimal migration script i ran: https://gist.github.com/emma/redwood-brew-migrate — includes detection and safe symlink creation. posting here in case it helps others.

raj: thanks. can we add an entry in troubleshooting docs under devex/installer about this exact symptom + REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR workaround and the symlink hint? newbie-friendly steps w/ commands.

kelly: added a short draft to the docs PR queue. i'll ping y'all when ready for review. :sparkles:

emma: awesome, appreciate the speedy help. saved my demo for tomorrow. :relieved:
